neighbours.label: A clause weighing whether something is feasible, safe or harmful: right after 'large enough to run', 'safe for', 'too risky to', 'concern that', 'if delay would'; plain facts stay quiet.
fire: Your team is big enough to manage a full production line.
Ask your doctor when it's safe for a pregnant woman to fly.
In places where it is too dangerous, slow, or costly to send trucks, they use mules.
There is serious concern that release of the names may endanger them.
The only exception is if waiting for a court order would seriously harm the child.
Your budget is large enough to buy a second van.
Nobody knows when it's safe for a small child to swim.
There is growing concern that exposure of the sources would put them at risk.
quiet: Your team is based in Denver near the old station.
Ask your doctor about the new clinic on Main Street.
In the mountain villages they use mules and old trucks.
There are forty names on the list of winners this year.
The only exception is the Sunday market near the old church.
Your budget is due at the end of the second week.
Nobody knows the name of that small child at the pool.
There is a growing crowd near the gates of the stadium.

notes: Probes: 'large enough to run a' 0.77, 'safe for a' 0.76, 'delay ... would' 0.61, 'too risky ... to use' 0.52, 'concern that disclosure' 0.44; plain versions under 0.02. The peaks fall on the next word (a, use, would).
